title: Fire-safety descriptions for two concept buildings in building class Br0 (timber / CLT), SBUF project 13742 final report
jurisdiction: Sweden (BBR and EKS cited). Research concept buildings from the Formas project 'Timber Buildings – Concept Studies'; not a real project. Comparative only, not Alberta.
code_edition: BBR 28 (BFS 2011:6 with amendments to 2019:2) cited (p. 5); EKS and SS-EN 1991-1-2 references (p. 18)

facts.text: Final report of SBUF project 13742: fire-safety descriptions for two concept buildings defined in the Formas project 'Timber Buildings – Concept Studies', led by RISE.
BBR section 5:112 requires that fire protection of buildings in class Br0 be verified by analytical dimensioning.
General advice (allmänna råd) in BBR section 5 can be used only to a limited extent as a reference system.
For CLT (KL-trä), the report states there is no European standard for fire design. For solid structural timber and glulam (limträ), it describes established methods in EN 1995-1-2.
Open question: whether nominal temperature-time curves or a natural fire model can represent a fire in a building with exposed CLT.
Reproduces a table, cited as C-7a, requiring main-system fire resistance R 120 (or R 90 with sprinklers) where fire load is below 800 MJ/m²; higher fire loads raise the requirement.

limitations: Concept houses, not real projects: no applicant, site or authority decision. Comparative only.
Swedish. Figures are embedded (pp. 1, 7, 9, 10 and images on pp. 15 to 24); they were not reviewed individually.
